papers.title: Detecting and Preventing Data Poisoning Attacks on AI Models
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the critical issue of data poisoning attacks on AI models, a growing concern in the ever-evolving landscape of artificial intelligence and cybersecurity. As advanced technology systems become increasingly prevalent across various sectors, the need for robust defence mechanisms against adversarial attacks becomes paramount. The study aims to develop and evaluate novel techniques for detecting and preventing data poisoning attacks, focusing on both theoretical frameworks and practical applications. Through a comprehensive literature review, experimental validation using the CIFAR-10 and Insurance Claims datasets, and the development of innovative algorithms, this paper seeks to enhance the resilience of AI models against malicious data manipulation. The study explores various methods, including anomaly detection, robust optimization strategies, and ensemble learning, to identify and mitigate the effects of poisoned data during model training. Experimental results indicate that data poisoning significantly degrades model performance, reducing classification accuracy by up to 27 % in image recognition tasks (CIFAR-10) and 22 % in fraud detection models (Insurance Claims dataset). The proposed defence mechanisms, including statistical anomaly detection and adversarial training, successfully mitigated poisoning effects, improving model robustness and restoring accuracy levels by an average of $15-20 \%$. The findings further demonstrate that ensemble learning techniques provide an additional layer of resilience, reducing false positives and false negatives caused by adversarial data injections. The findings of this paper contribute to the broader understanding of adversarial machine learning and provide actionable insights for practitioners in industries facing emerging threats to AI-based systems. By addressing the challenges of data poisoning attacks, this study aims to improve the security and reliability of AI models, ultimately fostering greater trust in AI technologies across critical applications.

papers.title: Robust and Adaptive Dual-Defense Framework Against Data Poisoning Attacks in Recommendation Systems
papers.abstract: Deep learning-based recommendation systems are highly vulnerable to data poisoning attacks, where adversaries manipulate user interactions to degrade model integrity. We hypothesize that combining an active robust loss with a passive GAN-based detection will significantly reduce poisoning impact in recommendation systems without sacrificing utility. We propose a robust and adaptive dual-defense framework: the active defense integrates a crafted loss function to mitigate poisoning effects while maintaining model performance. The passive defense employs a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)-based detection model to identify and filter poisoned data, enhancing detection accuracy and system security. The framework supports classical matrix factorization (MF) model and large language model (LLM)-based pipelines and scales to large datasets. Extensive experiments across multiple real-world datasets at varying poison rates show that our method outperforms representative defenses, consistently reducing attack success without sacrificing recommendation quality. The framework also admits a federated instantiation, where robust training and GAN-based detection run on clients and only privacy-preserving summaries are aggregated. The proposed method significantly improves the robustness and adaptability of recommendation systems under data poisoning attacks.

papers.title: Towards Imperceptible and Robust Adversarial Example Attacks against Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Machine learning systems based on deep neural networks, being able to produce state-of-the-art results on various perception tasks, have gained mainstream adoption in many applications. However, they are shown to be vulnerable to adversarial example attack, which generates malicious output by adding slight perturbations to the input. Previous adversarial example crafting methods, however, use simple metrics to evaluate the distances between the original examples and the adversarial ones, which could be easily detected by human eyes. In addition, these attacks are often not robust due to the inevitable noises and deviation in the physical world. In this work, we present a new adversarial example attack crafting method, which takes the human perceptual system into consideration and maximizes the noise tolerance of the crafted adversarial example. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed technique.

papers.title: Robust Real-World Image Super-Resolution against Adversarial Attacks
papers.abstract: Recently deep neural networks (DNNs) have achieved significant success in real-world image super-resolution (SR). However, adversarial image samples with quasi-imperceptible noises could threaten deep learning SR models. In this paper, we propose a robust deep learning framework for real-world SR that randomly erases potential adversarial noises in the frequency domain of input images or features. The rationale is that on the SR task clean images or features have a different pattern from the attacked ones in the frequency domain. Observing that existing adversarial attacks usually add high-frequency noises to input images, we introduce a novel random frequency mask module that blocks out high-frequency components possibly containing the harmful perturbations in a stochastic manner. Since the frequency masking may not only destroys the adversarial perturbations but also affects the sharp details in a clean image, we further develop an adversarial sample classifier based on the frequency domain of images to determine if applying the proposed mask module. Based on the above ideas, we devise a novel real-world image SR framework that combines the proposed frequency mask modules and the proposed adversarial classifier with an existing super-resolution backbone network. Experiments show that our proposed method is more insensitive to adversarial attacks and presents more stable SR results than existing models and defenses.

literature_themes.theme: Defending AI Models Against Data Poisoning Attacks
literature_themes.summary: This cluster of papers focuses on the detection and prevention of data poisoning attacks on AI models, particularly in the contexts of image recognition and recommendation systems. The studies propose various innovative frameworks and techniques, such as anomaly detection, robust optimization, and dual-defense mechanisms combining active and passive strategies, to enhance the resilience of AI systems against malicious data manipulation. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in model performance and security against poisoning attacks.
literature_themes.limitations: The cluster lacks comprehensive exploration of the long-term effectiveness of the proposed defenses in dynamic environments and does not address the potential trade-offs between model performance and security in depth. Additionally, one paper does not provide an abstract, limiting insights into its contributions.
literature_themes.gap_relevance: This cluster highlights the critical need for robust defense mechanisms in AI against evolving adversarial threats, thus supporting research gap identification in the areas of adaptive defense strategies and the integration of security measures in AI model training.

literature_themes.theme: Adversarial Robustness in Deep Learning Applications
literature_themes.summary: This cluster investigates methods to enhance the robustness of deep learning models against adversarial attacks, focusing on the development of imperceptible adversarial examples and robust image super-resolution techniques. The first paper introduces a new adversarial example crafting method that considers human perception to minimize detectability, while the second paper presents a framework that utilizes frequency domain analysis to mitigate the impact of adversarial noise in image super-resolution tasks.
literature_themes.limitations: Both studies highlight the challenge of balancing adversarial robustness with the preservation of image quality. The proposed methods may still struggle with certain types of adversarial attacks and may not generalize well across all datasets or applications. Additionally, the reliance on frequency domain techniques may introduce new artifacts or degrade performance in clean images.
literature_themes.gap_relevance: This cluster provides insights into the ongoing challenges of adversarial attacks in deep learning, particularly in real-world applications. It identifies the need for further research into more sophisticated adversarial detection and mitigation strategies that can maintain performance while ensuring robustness against evolving adversarial techniques.

summary: The literature on robust AI systems against data poisoning and adversarial attacks reveals two primary themes: the development of defense mechanisms against data poisoning, particularly in image recognition and recommendation systems, and enhancing adversarial robustness in deep learning applications. While various innovative frameworks have shown promise in improving model resilience, gaps remain in their long-term effectiveness and adaptability across diverse datasets. Future research should focus on creating adaptive defense strategies that balance performance and security, particularly in dynamic environments.
literature_tension_graph: The existing literature presents a tension between the effectiveness of dual-defense frameworks against data poisoning attacks and the long-term adaptability of these defenses across diverse datasets. While P2 claims significant success in maintaining recommendation quality, it lacks validation in federated learning contexts, suggesting a potential limitation in its generalizability (evaluation conflict). Additionally, P1 highlights improvements in model performance but does not address the trade-offs between security and performance in dynamic environments, indicating an unresolved condition regarding the balance of these factors (mechanism conflict). This suggests a research direction focused on developing adaptive defense strategies that can maintain robustness while ensuring performance across varying datasets and conditions.
scholarly_positioning: Existing research on robust AI systems has predominantly focused on developing defense mechanisms against data poisoning and adversarial attacks, yet significant gaps remain in the long-term effectiveness and adaptability of these strategies across diverse datasets. While frameworks like dual-defense mechanisms and frequency domain analysis have shown promise, they often overlook the trade-offs between model performance and security, particularly in dynamic environments. This proposed research aims to address these unresolved tensions by developing adaptive defense strategies that not only enhance robustness but also maintain performance across varying conditions. By situating this work within the broader debate on AI security, it seeks to contribute novel insights into the integration of resilience and efficiency in AI model training.
domain_router: machine-learning method development; The appropriate methodology template includes ablation studies to evaluate the effectiveness of adaptive defense strategies against data poisoning and adversarial attacks, alongside benchmark evaluations to assess model performance and security trade-offs across diverse datasets.
research_scope: This study will investigate the effectiveness of an adaptive dual-defense framework against data poisoning and adversarial attacks in image recognition models, specifically targeting convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The evaluation period will span six months, during which the model's performance will be assessed across multiple datasets, including CIFAR-10 and ImageNet. A control group will consist of standard CNNs without the proposed adaptive defenses. Primary outcomes will include accuracy and resilience metrics against both data poisoning and adversarial attacks, while secondary outcomes will focus on the trade-offs between model performance and security. The study aims to provide insights into the long-term effectiveness and adaptability of defense mechanisms in dynamic environments.

No hidden state extraction is necessary as the focus is on model performance rather than internal representations. The study does not require human participants or ethics approval since it does not involve user trust assessments. However, to enhance the robustness of the findings, it may be beneficial to include additional diverse datasets for better generalizability. Overall, the design is sound, but expanding the dataset variety would strengthen the study.

It is empirically testable through the proposed methodology of evaluating convolutional neural networks across multiple datasets. This topic is likely to garner committee interest due to its relevance in enhancing AI security, a pressing concern in the field. However, the strongest reason for potential rejection could be the lack of clarity on how the proposed framework significantly differs from existing solutions. To enhance the depth and research-worthiness, the problem could be reframed to explicitly focus on the mechanisms by which adaptability is achieved and measured, rather than just the effectiveness of the defenses themselves.

theoretical_mechanism: The proposed research investigates the adaptive dual-defense framework as the independent variable, which aims to enhance the resilience of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) against data poisoning and adversarial attacks. The mediator in this mechanism is the model's ability to dynamically adjust its defenses based on real-time data characteristics, influencing the dependent variable, which is the long-term performance and resilience of the CNNs. The theoretical framework is grounded in the concept of adaptive learning systems that can evolve based on environmental changes. The causal chain suggests that as the adaptive dual-defense framework is implemented, it leads to improved resilience metrics, thereby reducing the unsafe response rate of the models. System-level outcomes include enhanced accuracy and resilience against attacks, while user-level outcomes may involve increased trust and satisfaction due to perceived robustness. Assumptions requiring empirical validation include the effectiveness of the adaptive mechanisms in diverse datasets and the correlation between system resilience and user satisfaction.
hypothesis: The implementation of an adaptive dual-defense framework (independent variable) in convolutional neural networks (CNNs) will result in significantly higher long-term performance and resilience (primary dependent variable) against data poisoning and adversarial attacks compared to standard CNNs without such defenses (comparison/control), mediated by the model's ability to dynamically adjust its defenses based on real-time data characteristics.

Claim Boundaries:
The study claims that the adaptive dual-defense framework improves CNN resilience and performance over time, but it cannot conclude causation without controlling for confounding variables. Additionally, the results may not generalize to all types of AI systems or datasets beyond those tested.

The study cannot conclude that the adaptive dual-defense framework will be universally effective across all datasets or in all real-world scenarios, nor can it determine the specific mechanisms by which dynamic adjustments influence performance without further investigation.
methodology: This study will implement an adaptive dual-defense framework in convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to evaluate its effectiveness against data poisoning and adversarial attacks. The research will utilize CIFAR-10 and ImageNet datasets, with a control group consisting of standard CNNs without adaptive defenses. Key operationalized variables include long-term performance (measured through accuracy metrics) and resilience (assessed via resilience metrics). Evaluation will occur monthly over a six-month period, allowing for comprehensive analysis of model performance and adaptability. Statistical reasoning will involve comparing the performance of adaptive CNNs against the control group using appropriate metrics to ensure validity. Confounding variables such as dataset variability will be monitored to enhance reproducibility and control scope. The study aims to provide insights into the long-term effectiveness of the proposed defenses in dynamic environments.

proposal: This proposal defends the claim that implementing an adaptive dual-defense framework in convolutional neural networks (CNNs) significantly enhances their long-term performance and resilience against data poisoning and adversarial attacks compared to standard CNNs. The long-term adaptability of dual-defense frameworks across diverse datasets remains unresolved, particularly as existing studies do not adequately address the trade-offs between performance and security, nor do they validate the effectiveness of these frameworks in dynamic environments. This research introduces a novel adaptive dual-defense framework that dynamically adjusts its defenses based on real-time data characteristics, which is expected to improve model robustness against evolving adversarial threats. The framework's mechanism is grounded in adaptive learning principles, allowing CNNs to respond to data variations, thereby enhancing resilience metrics. The falsifiable hypothesis posits that CNNs with the adaptive dual-defense framework will demonstrate significantly higher long-term performance and resilience against data poisoning and adversarial attacks compared to standard CNNs without such defenses. The strongest baseline for comparison will be standard CNNs without adaptive defenses, ensuring a rigorous evaluation of the proposed framework's effectiveness. A negative result would suggest that the adaptive mechanisms do not universally improve resilience, challenging the theoretical premise of adaptability in AI systems. To enhance methodological rigor, the proposal will include explicit operational definitions for constructs such as 'long-term performance' (measured through accuracy metrics over six months) and 'resilience' (assessed via resilience metrics against specific attack types). The evaluation will utilize CIFAR-10 and ImageNet datasets, with controls for confounding variables monitored throughout the study. This approach ensures comprehensive analysis and robust findings, directly addressing reviewer concerns regarding clarity and empirical justification for causal claims.
